Treatment at the Saugus WRP consists of influent screening, primary sedimentation, activated sludge biological treatment...
activated sludge biological treatment with nitrification and denitrification... biological nutrient removal system with a nitrogen denitrification process (NDN) in operation since September 2003

...secondary sedimentation, dual media pressure filtration, disinfection (UV and/or chloramination), and dechlorination as needed.
Hypochlorite and ammonia are used to disinfect treated effluent at the Saugus WRP... the chloramination disinfection system will be retained as a backup disinfection process.
SCVSD installed the UV disinfection system at the Saugus WRP on July 20, 2021
Treated wastewater discharged to Santa Clara River is dechlorinated with sodium bisulfite, to remove residual chlorine when chloramines are used as the disinfecting agent.
Waste activated sludge from both the Saugus and Valencia WRPs is thickened by dissolved air flotation.
Thickened waste activated sludge and primary sludge are combined, digested anaerobically, dewatered and then reused through composting.
